findings.cause: Git observer executable entrypoint bypasses fresh Root GO, original clock, Root authority and canonical lock.
findings.proof: Observer __main__ calls envelope/private_dir and environment checks, accepts add/commit/push, saves a receipt and execve Git. Its load_go definition is never called by this entrypoint. No GO argument, intent/parent publisher birth validation, canonical lock check or original CLOCK binding is required before execve. Static counterexample: under the prescribed Git caps, private ACTUAL_DAILY and benign observer environment, its documented argv shape can select commit/push while ROOT-GO.json is absent. This counterexample was NOT executed. Publisher-side pinning protects the normal caller path but does not guard this independently executable helper entrypoint.
findings.required_change: Make every observer exec require exact bound Root GO/clock/Source and verified publisher custody/intent for this argv under the existing canonical lock; reject a direct/unbound invocation before any Git exec. Clip the actual observer GNU budget to the original clock. Preserve existing bounded actual birth/stdio receipts.

findings.cause: README preimage custody is dropped between checking the path and truncating the opened file.
findings.proof: Line403 verifies the current path byte ref, then reservation writing occurs before safe_open. The opened fd at408 is checked only for regular/single-link/current owner at410, then truncated. A changed or replaced regular owner README inserted between those operations satisfies those checks and is overwritten; post-copy SHA checks verify only the newly written approved bytes. O_NOFOLLOW prevents symlinks but does not bind this fd to the verified preimage/inode. Static race witness only, no filesystem mutation or source execution.
findings.required_change: Bind the opened README fd and its inode/byte preimage to the verified expected README before destructive writing, recheck custody immediately before truncation, and refuse/preserve intervening owner changes. Carry an exact preimage/custody receipt through the copy reservation.

findings.cause: Direct GNU wait is treated as sufficient to seal and unlink streams before checking whether observed producers remain.
findings.proof: Publisher selects final spool_seal solely on direct_wait or cleanup_direct_wait at320; known owned birth observations and rejection occur later at323/326. Launcher makes the same choice at203 before its after-birth checks at206/209. spool_seal unlinks the original at106. If the directly waited GNU exits while an observed Git/publisher producer remains, the snapshot is sealed and original path deleted before the later refusal; continuing bytes are lost from the durable path. Protocol12 explicitly requires a surviving/unknown stream to stay provisional. Direct wait on a wrapper is not proof that descendants closed their inherited stream fds. Static failure witness only.
findings.required_change: Observe and prove relevant exact producer/owned birth closure before final sealing/unlinking. Any surviving or unconfirmed producer must retain the original spool and a labelled provisional snapshot. Preserve both direct wrapper wait and descendant closure evidence.

findings.cause: Exceptional cleanup lacks custody of the nested publisher/Git tree and excludes observed descendants solely because they have a different session.
findings.proof: Launcher samples its child GNU and that GNU direct children, records publisher self, and on failure signals only that pair. It never traverses publisher children or their nested Git GNU trees, although publisher creates Git groups with start_new_session=True at304. Publisher watch records recursive own births, but cleanup at275 skips every observed descendant whose session differs from the direct GNU session; captured parent/ownership evidence is discarded for that stop decision. A publisher failure/kill during an active nested Git or a known descendant that changes session can leave owned work running after the limited cleanup. Current code makes no exhaustive fork claim, which is correct, but this does not satisfy cleanup of the finite observed owned tree. Static failure witness only.
findings.required_change: Maintain finite exact PID/birth/boot/ancestry custody of observed nested descendants across launcher/publisher boundaries; stop only matching authorized owned births, children first, with protected writers/PID2306 excluded. Treat uncaptured/unknown descendants as STOP_UNCONFIRMED and retain their evidence, rather than equating wrapper wait with closure. Do not use broad process/group killing or create extra writers.

findings.cause: Secondary cleanup/sealing failures can replace and lose the original causal refusal.
findings.proof: git catches BaseException without capturing it in record. A cleanup/fsync/spool-seal error can replace that original failure. At the top level primary cause is stored only in memory until finish writes RESULT; if finish fails earlier while writing STEPS/COPIED/OWNED, fallback prints the sealing exception and prior_state but omits the original cause and prior causal receipt refs. A bounded final refusal such as authority/cap/custody failure can therefore disappear behind an I/O/sealing exception. No failure injection or source execution was performed.
findings.required_change: Capture primary failures before cleanup and preserve them independently from cleanup/sealing errors. Make the bounded fallback carry both causes and all durable partial causal refs, even when larger receipt sealing fails. Keep actual nonzero/unknown terminals and partial effects without retry.
